correctness.rationale: Every closed factor of a five-run word can be sorted by number of its constant runs. One-run factors and empty factor contribute 1+max(a,c,e)+max(b,d); two-run factors cannot have borders. Balanced end fragments give three-run terms x+y+z-I*h; four-run mixed borders give z(x+y). Five-run factors close either by a mixed border exactly when b=d and both zero end fragments fit the central zero run, contributing I*x*y, or by a pure-zero border when equal outer fragments exceed the middle zero run. The elementary identities reduce the sum to n+1+z(x+y)+I(xy-min(x,y)), with x=min(a,c), y=min(c,e), z=min(b,d). Since n>=1.5(x+y)+2z and xy<=(x+y)^2/4, the quadratic terms are <=n^2/8. Witness lengths (2k,k,2k,k,2k) attain 8k^2+6k+1, padding the last zero-run extends to every large n. The exact formula was algebraically reduced to the October 25 formula and tested on 243 tuples; finite checks are not universal proof.
